orig_text:
The updated SKEYSEED value is then used to derive the following
keying materials.

   {SK_d(1) | SK_ai(1) | SK_ar(1) | SK_ei(1) | SK_er(1) | SK_pi(1) |
    SK_pr(1)} = prf+ (SKEYSEED(1), Ni | Nr | SPIi | SPIr)

As per [RFC9242], both peers compute IntAuth_i1 and IntAuth_r1 using
the SK_pi(1) and SK_pr(1) keys, respectively.  These values are
required in the IKE_AUTH phase of the exchange.
correct_text:
The updated SKEYSEED value is then used to derive the following
keying materials.

   {SK_d(1) | SK_ai(1) | SK_ar(1) | SK_ei(1) | SK_er(1) | SK_pi(1) |
    SK_pr(1)} = prf+ (SKEYSEED(1), Ni | Nr | SPIi | SPIr)

As per [RFC9242], both peers compute IntAuth_i1 and IntAuth_r1 using
the SK_pi and SK_pr keys from IKE_SA_INIT (i.e., the value preceding the exchange),
respectively.  These values are required in the IKE_AUTH phase of the exchange.
notes:
RFC 9242 states that the keys used during epoch i are the keys from epoch (i-1). From RFC 9242, section 3.3.2: 

Each calculation of IntAuth_[i/r]* uses its own keys SK_p[i/r]*,
which are the most recently updated SK_p[i/r] keys available before
the corresponded IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange is started.
